assumptions.text: Four phases (joining, borrowing, settling, maintaining) drafted from the capabilities; the tool lifecycle is placed last because it is a branch, not the member's story.
Concession approval happens before the fee is paid (the rate decides the amount); the coordinator approves, not a desk volunteer.
Reservation expiry, due reminders, overdue marking, late-fee accrual and membership lapsing are all clock-fired; the schedules given are guesses.
A cash payment at the desk is the same Fee Paid event with method=cash; the volunteer records it. No separate cash ledger is stormed.
Inspection after a return only happens when the volunteer notes damage (manual policy); routine inspections are on a schedule not stormed at light depth.
Failure paths beyond a card decline (Stripe webhook late, item lost and never returned, member disputes a fee) are not on the timeline.

open_questions.text: Does a lost item (never returned) end as a damage charge at replacement value, and who declares it lost?
Is the late fee capped per loan at the item's replacement value, or per member across items?
Can a member reserve a second item while one reservation is pending, and does a pending reservation count toward the three-item limit?
Does an overdue item block renewal of the member's other loans?

notes_for_downstream.text: H1: 'Tool' (a catalogue kind: 'cordless drill', has a replacement value and safety notes) vs 'Item' (one asset-tagged physical unit with a condition and a status). Members reserve an item but talk about a tool; volunteers only ever handle items. Keep two terms, two owners.

Sharpens understand N2: on the board eligibility is read exactly once, by the desk volunteer at check-out (item-checked-out) via the member-standing read model. So one context (lending) consumes it and needs three facts from elsewhere: membership current (joining), balance zero (settling), no overdue and fewer than three items out (its own). Decompose must pick who assembles the answer.
Five clock-fired commands (lapse-memberships, expire-reservations, send-due-reminders, mark-loans-overdue, accrue-late-fee). Something must run on a schedule; it is not a user request.

H3: fee-paid can arrive from two channels (Stripe card, cash at desk) and card-payment-failed is reported by Stripe, possibly after the member has left the page. Payment confirmation is asynchronous from Stripe's side.

policies.name: Whenever membership fee paid, start the membership
Whenever a loan is overdue, accrue GBP 1 per day until returned or capped
Whenever an item is returned with damage noted, a maintenance volunteer inspects it
Whenever an item fails inspection after a loan, the coordinator decides a damage charge

hotspots.text: 'Tool' means the catalogue kind to a member browsing but the asset-tagged physical unit to a volunteer at the desk. Which one is reserved, and which one is retired?
Who answers 'may this member borrow?' at check-out - membership status, fee balance, overdue loans and item count live in three different parts of the flow.
Stripe may confirm or decline after the member has closed the page; cash is recorded by hand. Does the balance change on our record or on Stripe's word, and what if they disagree?
Is the 48-hour hold counted in calendar hours or only across desk opening days? A Sunday reservation would expire before the desk opens.
Nobody has said who declares an item lost after weeks overdue, or whether that ends as a damage charge at replacement value.

scenarios.name: Happy path: member reserves, collects and returns a drill on time
Late return: fee accrues, member pays online

glossary.definition: A resident household with a current membership; identified by a member number
A member's 12-month right to borrow, started when the annual fee is paid
A kind of thing the library lends ('cordless drill'), with a replacement value and safety notes; in the desk and workshop: the physical item (see Item)
One asset-tagged physical unit of a tool, with a condition and a status (available, reserved, on loan, in maintenance, retired)
A 48-hour hold on an available item for one member
One item in one member's hands from check-out to return, due in 14 days, renewable once by 7
The day a loan must be returned by; the day after it the loan is overdue
GBP 1 per item per overdue day, capped at the item's replacement value
What a member owes in late and damage fees; must be zero to borrow
A maintenance volunteer's safety and condition check of an item; pass or fail

plain_words.what: We laid out everything that happens in the tool library as a timeline of plain facts: a member joins, reserves, collects, returns; fees build up and get paid; tools come in, get inspected and retire.
plain_words.decided: 23 events in 4 phases. Four turning points: membership started, item checked out, item returned, fee paid. Five things happen on a clock, not because someone clicked.
plain_words.assumed: That 'tool' and 'item' are two different things (a kind versus one physical unit), and that a cash payment at the desk is just another way a fee gets paid.
plain_words.riskiest: If who-may-borrow is decided in three places instead of one, the library will let people borrow who owe money, and the two main goals slip.
